registered.maxAgeBasis:
Observed 58,510s (16h 15m), which is 195x the global 300s bound, so without an override native USDC prices nothing on this chain and /borrow is dead here. 90,000 is Constants.MAX_FEED_PRICE_AGE, the ceiling, leaving 31,490s (8h 45m) of headroom over the observation. Defensible because USDC is pegged — a day-old answer is wrong by basis points, not by percent — and this is the same number Sepolia's Chainlink USDC/USD carries for the same reason. Do not copy it onto a volatile feed to stop it reverting.
Stated plainly: 58,510s is ONE observation of an AGE, not a measurement of the publish INTERVAL. The interval is unknown and may exceed 90,000, in which case this feed will intermittently fail closed. That is now recoverable by any participant — PythPriceOracle.updatePrice is permissionless, so a borrower's own transaction can carry the update it needs — which is the reason a ceiling bound is acceptable here rather than a reason the staleness does not matter.

Same Crypto.USDC/USD feed as native USDC, so the same observation and the same ceiling bound. See the USDC entry above for why 90,000 is defensible for a pegged asset and must not be copied onto a volatile one.
